# MIR verifier mutation fixtures

`manifest-v0.json` defines verified named seeds, one fixture-local mutation per case, and the single expected `Vxxxx` rejection. The seed and entity labels are test vocabulary, not MIR block numbers, local numbers, source symbols, or a backend exchange format.

A runner must construct the named baseline, verify it successfully, confirm every target and optional supporting entity exists, clone it, apply exactly one mutation, and then require the complete verifier result to equal the one listed code. A baseline failure or extra verifier code is a fixture harness failure.

`schema-v0.json` rejects unknown fields and uses JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Arbitrary graph serialization, mutation cascades, fuzz-corpus encoding, and crash-bundle rendering remain separate contracts.

`internal/mirverifyfixture` executes all ten baselines and twenty-two isolated mutations through the same MIR verifier used after source lowering. The resource-definition mutation removes the `seed::Token` definition while leaving its resource local and isolates `V1001`; the tagged-type mutation removes the concrete Result construction type and separately isolates `V1001`. The normal-call mutation replaces its internal callee with an absent symbol and isolates `V1001` before artifact or backend handoff. The plain-region mutations remove reset or invalidate its exit kind and isolate `V1403`; the break-region-control mutation removes a `break` reset and isolates `V1403` before the loop-exit return. The checked-arithmetic mutation removes the addition marker and isolates `V1501` at the continuation operation. Passing this runner proves the listed v0 invariants and recipe isolation only; arbitrary malformed graphs, combined mutations, fuzzing, crash bundles, and backend-specific verification remain deferred.
